name: @w6w-apps/softr
description: Read and write records in a Softr app's own Database tables, manage its tables and users, over the Softr Database API and Studio Users API.

w6w.longDescription:
Softr lets you build internal tools, client portals and websites on top of a data source — most often its own built-in Softr Database, a native multi-table store with fields, views and (optionally) AI-assisted columns.

This app covers the Softr Database API end to end: list and inspect databases, tables and views, then read, search, create, update and delete the records inside a table. Search supports Softr's full filter grammar (binary/unary/ternary/composite conditions, relative date tokens), not just a flat equality match.

A second, separately-hosted surface — the Studio Users API — manages the people signed up to a published Softr app: create, delete, activate, deactivate and invite a user, generate a magic sign-in link, and trigger a user sync. It shares the same Personal Access Token as the Database API but talks to a different host and is scoped per-app by a domain header rather than by an app-scoped path.

One documented endpoint is deliberately not implemented: validating a Softr-issued user JWT (`POST /v1/api/users/validate-token`) is called against the Softr app's own live domain — a value that varies per app and per customer rather than a fixed API host — so it cannot be reached through a static network allowlist. See the README for the full reasoning.
